title: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management: insights and retention policy recommendations for sensitive SharePoint and OneDrive data
summary: Hold: the published retention-policy licences do not establish that the new insights and recommendations are included. The existing retention-policy guidance also omits that administrators restricted to administrative units cannot configure policies for SharePoint sites.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Existing Data Lifecycle Management retention policies cover Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Retention policies are the cornerstone for data lifecycle management. Use these policies for Microsoft 365 workloads that include Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Viva Engage.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Retention policies can retain content.
claims.quote: Configure whether content for these services needs to be retained indefinitely, or for a specific period if users edit or delete it.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A retention policy can permanently delete content after a specified period.
claims.quote: Or you can configure the policy to automatically permanently delete the content after a specified period if it's not already deleted.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Retention policies can combine retention with subsequent deletion.
claims.quote: You can also combine these two actions for retain and then delete, which is a very typical configuration.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Compliance Administrator role group is a documented way to grant permissions for creating and managing retention policies.
claims.quote: Members of your compliance team who will create and manage retention policies and retention labels need permissions to the Microsoft Purview portal. To grant permissions for this limited administration, we recommend that you add users to the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The role guidance for creating SharePoint retention policies gives Compliance Administrator or Retention Management but omits the qualification for administrators restricted to administrative units.
claims.quote: you won't be able to configure a retention policy that includes SharePoint sites or Exchange public folders. For these locations, you must be an unrestricted administrator.
claims.fix: Keep the documented role names, but append this qualification to the role guidance and controls[1].note in both front matter and the rendered table: "For policies that include SharePoint sites, the administrator must be unrestricted; administrators assigned administrative units cannot configure those policies." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: View-Only Retention Management is the documented read-only role for retention policies and labels.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using this default role, you can create a new role group and add the Retention Management role to this group. For a read-only role, use View-Only Retention Management.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The person configuring retention policies does not need access to the content.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create, configure, and apply retention policies and retention labels. The person configuring these policies and labels doesn't require access to the content.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is a separate role required for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Specific to priority cleanup that can override retention labels and policies when it's necessary to expedite the permanent deletion of sensitive information, admins must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. This role isn't included by default in the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The existing retention-policy creation entry point is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote: 1. Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. 2. Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration, and name your new retention policy.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "<policy name>" -SharePointLocation "<site URL>" creates a retention policy for the specified SharePoint site.
claims.quote:
New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "Regulation 123 Compliance" -ExchangeLocation "Kitty Petersen", "Scott Nakamura" -SharePointLocation "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/teams/finance"
This example creates a retention policy named "Regulation 123 Compliance"

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The new retention policy is not valid until a rule is added with New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). For more information, see New-RetentionComplianceRule.
